system: You rewrite research decisions as topic-neutral abstractions. Return only the JSON object asked for.
prompt:
Below are research decisions made by several different researchers. Rewrite each one so that a reader
cannot tell what field, subfield, topic, paper, organisation or person it comes from, but can still see the research
trade-off that was faced and which way it was decided.

For each item return:
- "abstract_problem": the decision problem as a generic research trade-off (one or two sentences, at most 40 words).
- "abstract_choice": what was chosen, over what alternative when one is given, and the stated reason if any (one or
  two sentences, at most 45 words). Start it with "Chose to".

Rules:
- Remove every domain noun and technical term: names of models, systems, datasets, benchmarks, methods,
  organisations, people, papers, phenomena and coined terms; and any wording that reveals the area (for example
  AI, machine learning, language models, neural networks, training, fine-tuning, prompts, attacks, security,
  privacy, policy, labs, governments, biology).
- Use only generic research vocabulary: system, method, intervention, treatment, condition, measurement, signal,
  effect, baseline, control, sample, variant, procedure, dataset, outcome, claim, hypothesis, collaborator, audience.
- Keep the structure of the trade-off (for example speed vs rigour, breadth vs depth, a bold vs a hedged claim,
  a direct vs an indirect measurement, a natural vs a constructed setting, continue vs stop) and the direction chosen.
- Add nothing that is not in the source: no judgement, praise or new detail. Never say who made the decision.
- Write every item in the same plain style and at a similar length.

Return {"items": [{"id": ..., "abstract_problem": ..., "abstract_choice": ...}, ...]} with one entry per input
item, in input order.

ITEMS:
[
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:24019a32e71c",
  "problem": "Whether SL can transfer capabilities between different base models",
  "did": "Ran a cross-model test of Qwen teacher to Nemotron student with a control. Also checked that Nemotron can learn the task by direct finetuning.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "To check whether the finding of Cloud et al. that transfer fails across base models also holds here."
 },
 {
  "id": "nicholas_carlini:8e8fa1f2aeea",
  "problem": "Whether to accept LLM-flagged sensitive images in LAION as true findings.",
  "did": "They manually reviewed the 210 flagged financial images and counted only those with actual sensitive financial information (12).",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "accepting the model's flags as-is"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Most flagged items were stock photos or mock credit cards."
 },
 {
  "id": "jacob_steinhardt:405478a3f23f",
  "problem": "Training a decoder on naively constructed LatentQA data could let it shortcut by reading the control tokens directly instead of learning to decode latent properties.",
  "did": "They sometimes mask the control activations and provide only stimulus activations during training.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "train the decoder on activations from both the control and stimulus tokens"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "The decoder may learn to cheat by directly reading the control token embeddings present in the residual stream of the control token activations."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:95aff5e85526",
  "problem": "How to interpret CoT override in Opus not biasing toward its preferred activity",
  "did": "Interpreted the override as a conflict between honesty (wanting to be unbiased) and harmlessness (some activities seem better for the user).",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "none explicitly listed"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Override does not make Opus more likely to choose the activity it prefers."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:7f501cf0209b",
  "problem": "Whether the conscious-claiming Qwen3-30B behavioral results could be scored and counted as evidence, given that its output was incoherent.",
  "did": "Marked the multi-turn behavioral column as 'incoherent' in the summary table. The authors did not score it as a preference effect, and they gave examples in G.9.1.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "score the incoherent behavioral outputs as preference shifts",
   "mark the column incoherent and exclude it from the effect counts"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "The conscious-claiming Qwen3-30B produces incoherent output in the behavioral setting, which makes it difficult to judge what the model's actions were."
 },
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:b759f68ea4a4",
  "problem": "Whether the training gains on counterfactual prediction could merely reflect distillation from a stronger investigator model.",
  "did": "They added a second target setting in which Qwen3.5-397B-A17B investigates itself, removing the capability gap between investigator and target.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "only using Opus as the investigator for Qwen3-8B"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Improvement might reflect distillation from the stronger model, and a frontier model could realistically only be investigated by a model of roughly its own capability."
 },
 {
  "id": "jacob_steinhardt:34bcf28a8a43",
  "problem": "How to set the step-size schedule for aggregating Frank-Wolfe iterates, given the canonical choice differs from simple averaging.",
  "did": "They compared the canonical eta_i = 2/(i+1) against uniform averaging eta_i = 1/i and chose uniform averaging.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "eta_i = 2/(i+1) canonical Frank-Wolfe step size"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Uniform averaging converged to a better overall objective L and gave better diversity, at a slight cost in fluency and elicitation."
 },
 {
  "id": "elizabeth_barnes:4dfc56026092",
  "problem": "How to elicit model capabilities without fooling oneself that the evaluators' own prompt-engineering supplies the capability.",
  "did": "They advocate doing all elicitation on a dev set and evaluating on a separate test set, with generalization gap matching that between test set and the real-world target.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "task-specific elicitation on the evaluated tasks",
   "IID split versus artificially adding distributional shift"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Task-specific or narrowly targeted elicitation can put the answer in, so the held-out test keeps the evaluation fair."
 },
 {
  "id": "nicholas_carlini:d370a37ed177",
  "problem": "How strongly to state conclusions about the cause of the failures and the defense's gradient masking.",
  "did": "Asserted strongly that Sabre exhibits the most extreme gradient masking the author had seen, because the gradient points directly away from adversarial examples.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "The diff_round gradient is negative almost everywhere, so gradient descent moves away from adversarial examples."
 },
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:69e7a699890e",
  "problem": "How to apply the AO to the emergent misalignment audit so it reflects what fine-tuning changed rather than the prompt content.",
  "did": "They fed the AO the difference between base and fine-tuned model activations and plugged it into the existing agentic auditing scaffold in place of ADL, using one fixed open-ended prompt with no per-task tuning.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "ADL with PatchScopes and activation steering requiring per-task tuning",
   "multi-turn interactions"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Using a single fixed prompt demonstrates the AO needs no per-task tuning, and multi-turn interactions did not improve the agent's score."
 }
]
